en: The Buddha spoke this Scripture of the Divine Talismans of the Seven Thousand Buddhas:
it causes the human body to extend its years and increase its lifespan. One shall reach the age of one hundred and twenty; in the year Jiachen, [the lifespan] shall further increase.
The seven thousand buddhas will protect the human body, ensuring that one does not encounter evil [omens].
□ Save me and increase my lifespan.
May the seven thousand Buddhas protect this human body and sever all [obstacles]... □□□□ Jiazi year.
From the Buddha, may the lifespan of this human body be increased for those whose lives are coming to an end.
May the thousand Buddhas who descend to be born [in this world] grant me an increase in my lifespan.
May the seven thousand Buddhas who protect those who [practice] the *nien-fo* [recollection of the Buddha] increase their lifespan. Seven hundred and seventy Buddhas shall descend to be born.
Grant me an increase in my lifespan.
Among the seven hundred and seventy Buddhas who descend as incarnate bodies,
may the Bodhisattva subdue the Māras of those afflicted by illness.
The thirty-five Buddhas descend to birth and increase my lifespan;
seven hundred and seventy Buddhas protect the human body.
May they attain firm and courageous diligence; may the fifty-three Buddhas descend to be born in this world and grant me an increase in my lifespan.
May they protect my human life for seven hundred and seventy billion years, so that I may constantly attain the Way of the Buddha.
The six Buddhas descend to birth and grant me an increase in my lifespan;
seven hundred and seventy Buddhas protect people and augment their physical lives.
Open wisdom relies upon unimpeded penetration.
May the seven Buddhas who descend to birth grant me increased longevity;
may the thirty-five Buddhas protect and guide human beings.
My deportment is flawless;
the various māras naturally stand in awe.
Eighty thousand bodhisattvas have increased my lifespan.
The vows of seventy-three Buddhas, as well as those of all the Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas seeking Pratyekabuddhahood—
may these Arhats, acting as disciples, increase their lifespans.
May the seven thousand Buddhas subdue and smelt away the various Māras, sorcerers, mountain forests, local deities, and the spirits of the northern banks, so that they are all utterly extinguished.
The talisman of the Thousand Buddhas smelts and subdues the wind-kings, the hearth-lords, the water-dragons, and the earth-spirits; they are all utterly extinguished.
The talisman of the Thousand Buddhas smelts and subdues the five depletions, the six sighs, evil dreams, lamentations, wild paths, and curses; they are all utterly extinguished.
The star Po-jun presides over depletion and emptiness;
the star Wu-qu presides over official affairs;
the star Lien-cheng presides over verbal disputes.
The Wenqu Star presides over evil dreams;
the Lucun Star presides over the hundred ghosts;
the Jumen Star ordains non-corporeal spirits.
The star Tanlang presides over evil qi.
It is recorded in the life-force within the Big Dipper;
it is recorded among the hundred ghosts within the Big Dipper.
The Three Terrace Stars protect one's person and life:
the first is the Star of Enmity, the second is the Star of Goodness,
and the third is the Star of Exorcism.
The fourth is the planet Venus;
the fifth is the constellation Śravaṇā, which can eliminate calamities and hardships,
and ward off pestilence and disease throughout the world.
May all those who commit illicit acts,
malevolent spirits, and wandering ghosts depart to tens of thousands of miles away.
Act with the utmost urgency, as required by the sacred edict.
The first is the talisman for opening the mind;
the second is the talisman for increasing one's lifespan;
the third is the talisman for protecting one’s body and life.
The fourth is the Talisman of the Non-Engraving of Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, and Earth.
The fifth is the Talisman of Exhausting the Spirits of the Ancestral Ghosts Who Cause Birth and Death;
when all the evil entities that cause such births see this talisman, they [are subdued].
Disperse and extinguish! Swiftly, as per the ritual command (*lùlìng*).
The General resides in the position of Zi.
On the twentieth day, Guichou, of the first month of the sixth lunar month, which begins on Renzi, the opening is revealed.
The Divine Talisman of the Thousand Buddhas protects and requests a hundred-year lifespan.
Whether it be a decline of the month, a decline of the day,
a decline of the year, or a decline of the season.
After one has received and worn this talisman, there shall be no further misfortunes or taboos regarding the days of the week.
This talisman of the Thousand Buddhas suppresses calamities and enables the person to transcend disasters, prolonging their years and increasing their lifespan;
once the talisman is received, their life span shall be extended.
The divine talisman for requesting longevity from the seven thousand Buddhas:
may one receive a lifespan of one hundred and twenty years,
with the tally of years fully complete according to this talisman.
Regarding this physical body:
after wearing the talisman,
all Buddhas give birth to me.
The various scriptures record me;
light illumines me;
and the yin and yang nurture me.
The four seasons nourish me;
the five elements carry me;
the five clouds cover me.
The Bodhisattvas protect me;
six hundred sexagenary cycles cover me;
the Five Emperors assist me.
The five musical instruments attend me;
the five weapons guard me;
the celestial bodies align with me.
Five silken threads rest upon me;
five fragrant incenses perfume me;
I recline upon a golden couch.
A brocade quilt covers me;
immortals support me;
jade maidens attend me.
The Blue Dragon leads me;
the White Tiger confines me;
the guards of the lords and marquises receive me.
The five classes of people revere me;
the myriad people honor me;
the elders follow my lead.
The people of my village shall be affectionate toward me;
bows, arrows, blades, weapons, and bandits shall stay far from me;
tigers, wolves, vipers, and snakes shall avoid me.
The five poisons and the arts of sorcery shall avoid my person.
Once these talismans are worn, the heavens open up in the four directions,
and the hundred ghosts shall not follow me.
Falling into water, one does not drown;
encountering weapons or soldiers, one is not harmed;
in all comings and goings, there is auspiciousness and excellence.
One shall not encounter calamities or misfortunes.
Protected by the Generals of the Four Quarters and the Five Peaks,
one will possess every form of spiritual power.
Baoshuan was ahead of me;
Xian harbored respect for me and gave me excellent medicine.
The divine talisman protects me;
the hundred ghosts avoid me;
the hundred deities love me.
The Gate of Heaven opened for me;
the Portal of Earth brought me forth;
the cool spring gave me drink.
The Masters of Wind, Frost, and Rain cleared the way.
Those who encountered the talisman head-on died;
those who opposed the talisman perished.
Amulets for suppressing the ghosts of death and mourning, both old and new, including those of Yin and Yang, those who bring calamity, and those who lie in wait;
amulets for suppressing the ghosts of mountains, forests, and the altars of soil and grain;
amulets for suppressing the ghosts that roam the heavens.
The talisman subdues the ghosts of the red-tongued ones.
The talisman subdues the ghosts of the five earths that dwell in neighboring houses.
The talisman subdues the ghosts of the daily-wandering terrestrial vapors.
Amulets to suppress the ghosts of those who died by the stars;
amulets to suppress the ghosts of those who died as travelers;
amulets to suppress the ghosts of those who died by the sword or in prison.
After my disciple wore the talisman of the thousand Buddhas,
he traveled forth in four directions,
his path extending infinitely in a thousand ways.
Ten thousand paths will be free of difficulty;
one shall not have nightmares while sleeping,
and whatever is sought shall always be attained.
May all wishes be fulfilled according to one's heart.
The teachings of the thousand Buddhas are as true as a tally.
May all that is commanded be executed with the utmost urgency, in accordance with the ritual decree.

First, the Talisman for Opening the Mind; second, the Talisman for Increasing the Life-Span; third, the Talisman for Protecting Body and Life; fourth, the Talisman for Ensuring Metal, Wood, Water, and Earth Do Not Harm One Another; fifth, the Talisman for Exhausting the Spirits of Ancestral Ghosts and Dead Demons Who Haunt Living Beings; the talisman for suppressing the ghosts of old and new deaths and the male and female spirits of hidden influence; the talisman for suppressing the ghosts of the three generations; the talisman for suppressing the ghosts that roam in heaven; the talisman for suppressing the ghosts of the red-tongued fire; the talisman for suppressing the ghosts of the five earths of the neighborhood; the talisman for suppressing the ghosts of the wandering breath of the soil; the talisman for suppressing the ghosts of those who die under the stars; the talisman for suppressing the ghosts of those who die as guests; the talisman for suppressing the ghosts of those who die by the sword or in prison; the talisman for suppressing the ghosts of boundary-omens and female omens; and the talisman for suppressing the ghosts of the innocent.
The Scripture on the Divine Talismans of Seven Thousand Buddhas Spoken by the Buddha.
